comment: I have a reactive dog and the trails don't have a lot of space to pull her away from other dogs but we had an amazing time regardless!
mosquitoes friendly

Its a beautiful trail, easy to find your way around. I would not using “all” of your water to make cup noodles (they were worth it tho). 

Saw a little unbothered wild porcupine, chill guy. The hike can get challenging at times but it gives to time to recover, the lakes carry this hike for me!
Beautiful day , smallest bit of mud near ponds but nothing to write home about !!
Totally worth it, It’s medium to easy hike. I would suggest to hold a stick when Hiking , and start with Clif Top trail then Lookout trail. It will take 2 hours and a half.
Great hike
Bring spikes very icy in spots.
Snowy
Deep snow on trail with some more packed than others.  Beautiful winter views.
Amazing!

Beautiful winter weather, stairs were covered in snow but able to walk up/down them carefully (with proper boots and spikes). Jacobs’s ladder look put not well labeled, it’s no the same as the stairs lookout
The gate was open!  Was it an early Xmas present?  Maybe…:-)
Mostly easy trail with section that were moderate.

Relatively easy to follow, but check in with your downloaded map periodically. Not too busy once you’ve passed the initial multi-trail head. 
Mostly covered by the canopy but sun in the clearings, so be prepared.
Amazing forest views and lookout point .
Always a good time and a fun park. The rock stairs and the lookout next to it are always the busiest part. The rest is generally pretty empty, including the superior look out.
Great hike on a fine day.
Great loop. Not too crowded. Parking app a bit finicky. Staff at gate checking reservations. Tons of birds identified.
It was our first time on the trail. Beautiful scenery! Trails can be muddy and/or icy this time of year. We wore crampons the whole time.
Good hike
Lots of snow. Lake not fully frozen yet
Well cleared trails, beautiful trees and no ice! Easy enjoyable hike.
Washrooms on the trail are closed, please use them at Parking Lot before heading to the trail.
Snowy today, but well tracked in. Vault privies *not* awesome.
Awesome trail 8 bucks to get in good hiking boots. Great views, french sax, and lots of water
Very easy to walk and the trail is well maintained.  A quiet and beautiful walk. The apps estimated time for the walk might be too optimistic. Realistically, give yourself 2.5 hrs.
It was slammed on a Monday afternoon during work hours. After peak colours. Granted it was a beautiful day but still kinda nuts. Still beautiful. Did not complete full loop due to arriving late.
Have to book parking pass for the Centre parking.
Watch out for horse poop. Gorgeous fall colours. Beautiful view. Cool rock formations
This trail was not that busy in the morning. We went at 9 in the morning but we passed a lot of people on our way back. Totally worth it.
Beautiful park!
rocks were cool, but not as many as expected. some nice inclines at parts. maps a bit confusing to follow at some points. lookout was pretty nice! i liked the sand at the beggining

Very easy hike, pretty flat for the most part. we didn't follow this route for the whole hike. Took different paths to see the cliffs. it is a little disappointing, maybe about 10-20m of the trail is actually on the cliffs/caves? Mosquitoes were huge so bring bug spray. washrooms are available at trailhead and somewhere within the trail.
Great trail.  Some incline but very enjoyable. Saw turtles and frogs at the lakes
Not a lot of leaves yet at this time of the year yet.
Beautiful at this time of the year!
Mud! lots of it!!!! But it was fun and  beautiful!¡

This is the best "Short" trail in the park. Basically, add the rock cliffs and main observation deck to this hike (only a few mins out of the way) and it's kind of a "Mono Cliffs Greatest Hits", even if you don't get to walk along the sublime escarpment trail. Surprisingly the conditions aren't that muddy today. It's just not as pretty as summer or fall due to the shoulder season.
Amazing day for a hike. Took a different route than usual. Nice to see the lookout. Will have to come back in fall.
Great conditions early, got a little slippery as the morning warmed up.
Did an out and back to see the viewing platforms. Was decent but Boyne had better views and was free. No major inclines/declines and lookout points were decent, cliffs were cool.
Moderate trails, beautiful lookout platform.

Busy trail even for Monday. Automatic gates,so you need to register before entering. Beautiful trail though. There are johnny on the spots before you begin trail. Trail has lots of off shoots so follow trail map.
Great trail for some amazing fall views!  Nice taking more of the side trails.
Despite some rain, trail was solid. Pre-book your reservation! Park was full, and if we hadn't reserved, we wouldn't have got in.

Calm and easy hike. A little elevation at one or two points on the way but mainly a flat trail. Paths are wide and well-maintained. Encountered one porcupine bobbling away, at least 5 Garter snakes, butterflies, honeybees and centipedes (i think). Lots of apples on the trail and trees. Fall colours have started to show up so the view from the top was colourful. Weather was perfect on the day, not too not too cold and no bugs!
Amazing hike, worth the climb to the lookout!

Calm and easy hike. A little elevation at one or two points on the way but mainly a flat trail. Paths are wide and well-maintained. Encountered one porcupine bobbling away, at least 5 Garter snakes, butterflies, honeybees and centipedes (i think). Lots of apples on the trail and trees. Fall colours have started to show up so the view from the top was colourful. Weather was perfect on the day, not too hot not too cold and no bugs!

This was what I would call an easy hike with a few payoff locations.  Several lookouts and Jacob's ladder make it fun.   Pay for parking online before you go as the cell reception isn't very good at the lot.  Tons of other hikes are also on the property if you are adventurous.    You could even bike lots of them.     Have fun

We started at 8:30am. Very few bugs. We did register for parking the night before. It was a rainy day and we didn’t meet anyone on the trails.  Considering all the rain, it wasn’t too muddy. I wore running shoes and it was fine. Lookout is alright. Parts of the trail get very narrow. 
Definitely check out the canyon cliffs.  It’s a little off route from this trail.
Muddy but really an easy to moderate trail.
9.3-10  trail, be sure to turn right at the washrooms and take the trail to lookout peak is amazing! One of the best views I’ve seen this year. 18 parks done so far.
Nice trail. Your mostly in shade thanks to the trees but there are a lot of mosquitoes.
Great trail! It was a bit sunny at the start because we hiked at 12:30! But over all good!
Trail was muddy and icy on April 7. Wear suitable shoes.
Icy and slippery

Beautiful!  Took Carriage Trail all the way back to the car and going up the hill towards the west is quite the climb up with lots of snow and some icy spots especially near the stairs.  Would highly recommended coming to Mono Cliffs.  Such beautiful trails in the winter.

Not as pretty in the middle of winter but it's still nice. Especially the rocks and the lookout trail. I accidentally kept recording all the way to the Mono Brewery which is very close by, and honestly? Great beer I'd you enjoy that, give it a shot lol. Trail conditions are great on the cliff-top trail because that's where the rocks and platform are. The rest of it (Bruce Side trails for example) aren't as packed and can get a bit more slick with the current soft snow.
Icy in a small number of areas, mainly snow. Can access scenic rock cliffs (Jacob’s Ladder) from this route but is just slightly off trail.
Very easy for the most part. Some interesting spots around the steeper climbs, the ravine and the crack in the cliff (you can walk down the stairs to it, but it's a dead end)

Awesome trail. Really beautiful with all the changing colours and fallen leaves. When going to the Clifftop lookout, just before you get to the top, there is a set of stairs that go down, take that to see some really cool cliffs! Will definitely be back again!
Beautiful trail, well maintained, some of the most beautiful views of fall colours.

Great day! No bugs. Not too hot. Park warden at entrance so make sure you’ve reserved your spot online. Saw 2 park ambassadors picking up litter which I thought was great however it’s better if people didn’t  litter in the first place. Don’t be an entitled person and expect other people to clean up after you… PACK OUT your own garbage! If you “hide it” or throw it in the bushes it’s still littering and you’re a jerk.
As for the trail route… we loved this route! Some cool spots and occasionally great views.
The beginning is flat and okay but then the trail gets better with varying terrain and elevation. The latter was my favorite  nice trail.
Great hike, good for summer and better in fall with different colours
Great trail! Better to start early in the summer as it can get crowded.
Amazing trail - one of my favourite Ontario provincial parks I’ve done! Definitely a must do :)

Not overly challenging and is family friendly. Today (Sunday June 5) was VERY quiet which was nice.
Remember to reserve in advance as you will not be let in, regardless of how quiet the park may be.
Signage could be better as we didn’t know which way to get back to the parking lot.

Went without making a reservation, had to leave the park to book the parking where internet signal works, about 5 min away. It was Saturday 830am, was plenty of room.

Didn't go back to the loop after the lookout, and made a bigger loop, was fine with nice stairs downhill. Traffic was heavy, many group hikers along the way. You may have to take turns at the lookout.nWhen we completed the trail, parking was full around noon,. Do your  research in advance, as signals don't reach in the area.

Awesome trail with lots of variety and views. Arrived at 8am on a Tuesday and gate finally unlocked at 830am after two phone calls to the Mono Cliffs office.  Two of us at gate then and near noon only about a dozen cars. Maybe because it feels like 32°C.
Excellent day, beautiful trail
Awesome!
The actual part with the cliff walk through is really short. But it is an amazing trail took me about an hour and a half and I stopped for a bit at the lake
Good workout
Very wide trampled down trails. Not rugged like I thought it might be but the cliffs were really pretty! Was worth it!

I found this trail through a filter that included  " less likely to encounter others "- unfortunately on Easter Sunday there were over a 100 cars in the parking lot. fortunately the expanse of trails meant that only a few were encountered on the trail.with the exception of hawks there weren't many wildlife encounters , likely due to the heavy human traffic. The view from the look out the was okay but not fantastic ( viewed during the spring ). Also, when visiting during heavy traffic times ( long weekends etc) book online though the Ontario Parks website.
Muddy!

Tremendous trails!  Fantastic views.  Colourful cliff faces.  Forested trail sections with lots of elevation changes.  Some great view points over the valley gorge. Looking forward to summer visit after our microspikes winter trek. Lots of easy parking at entrance to site.
Great hike!
Well marked trails. Careful on the stairs, snow and ice covered right now.
Idiots give out tickets to people just trying to get some exercise. Probably covid related
For a winter hike, it was quite nice. Nice views, although it wasn’t the brightest day.  There are some slippery sections…be careful.
a little muddy, most paths had snow. not very slippery.
Great a bit muddy
A great loop! clear marked trail, I went on a Thursday morning and I saw a handful of people. beautiful autumn colours and easy terrain. would definitely go again!
Great lollipop loop! Some incline, wide path on busy spots, and great views. Make sure to reserve the parking spot.
Bunch of government cunts run this shit.  Don’t go
Beautiful changing terrain, well used, well marked. Hit the trail early before the crowds but as we were leaving the parking lot was full and lots of foot traffic heading in.
Disappointed.  Long boring hiking trails just to see a bit of lookout and wooden staircases.
Nice well groomed trails, not too difficult. Went on Monday, arrived before 11am hiked about 11kms in 3hrs. Parking lot was quite empty, not too many people.

Went to the right at the fork instead of going left that will lead towards the lookout point to avoid the crowd. Enjoyed the long way around and ended to a much better lookout by the boulders (not sure what that spot was called exactly)... Did the right decision to hike the long way first before going to where most people just end up seeing (the lookout and the scenic cliffs) coz there wasn’t a lot of people anymore by the time we got there. The trail was nice and shady, and some parts were like straight out of a thriller movie (lol) but the family liked it.

Great trail! Reservation is needed for entering any provincial parks now so number of people are limited. Not many people on the trail. We also didn't encounter many bugs which was such a relief. Hike was pretty shaded. The view is awesome! It is about 7 kms and we completed it in about 2.5 hrs. The toilet here is very unclean and full of bugs. We couldn't dare to use. This was by far the worst toilet among all the provincial parks we have been to.
Trail was great!! All trails needs to fix the trailhead entrance to the main parking lot. We had a blast hiking though!

Been here many times but this was the first time this year. Came on a weekday and it was quiet. The bugs were intense though… so wear a lot of bug spray. Hardly any litter…. Hooray! But it’s worth reminding people to pack out all garbage or use the garbage cans. Was super easy to reserve parking space online through provincial parks website. Will definitely come back to try a different hiking route.
it was long but
It was a nice shady trail with 15-22 degree today. We stopped at couple lake and pond points.
Great place!

Excellent walk to the lake. The lookouts were busy on a Saturday morning (sometime between 10-noon) but the actual trails were not. Once we got to the lake there were two groups picnicking but they were spread out. We saw thousands of tadpoles and a few bluejays.
Way too crowded.

it was great  very clean not  
many people   no  bugs
Such a great trail. So many splits and routes with beautiful scenery and heights.

Good family friendly trail. Fairly easy trail. Took my 8 month daughter in a carrier. Pretty decent effort to reward ratio. Was busy though.. Parking lot was full before 12pm.

This this hike would definitely be prettier w more foliage than seen in spring.. Autumn would probably be really good w the fall colours at one of the look out points on this trail.

The "stairs" between the rocks is pretty any season. Definitely saw a few Instagram savvy persons here.

Round trip w a baby and 45 min feeding  break took us 2.5hrs
Trails were drying nicely from some heavy rain earlier in the day.  Met 8-10 people on the trail.  This is a weekday trail for me, I avoid it due to the increased traffic on weekends.
Great trail. Well maintained. Dry. Busy.
All around good hike.
Great! Quite muddy
Sweet
A very nice trail. It is still icy this time of year (March)...so please bring icers. Saw many hikers struggling with icy trail. overall it was scenic and wonderful. highly recommended

My husband and I traveled this trail March 9th. We forgot to bring our crampons. After 2 days of 8 degrees the snow covered path was slushed enough to walk without slipping (in most areas.) The wooded areas were still quite slippery, as were the stairs leading down to the large rock formations. We just made sure to be extra careful in these areas. Over all - hike was good, weather was beautiful! Will definitely come back in the spring and explore other trails in this park/area and spend more time adventuring in and around the actual escarpment. 

Parking lot is a paid lot (even in winter). Theres a machine to print parking ticket  for dash. $7.50 for 4 hours, or full day (forget full day charge). Internet connection/gps signal was not great throughout the park, or in the general vacinity, so it might be a good idea to know which trails you plan on taking. There are lots of signs thought the park - but some of this trail takes you off of the map. Also when we left the park we wernt sure which direction to drive and couldnt get GPS signal. It took us a bit of driving before we were able to get connection. (and we tried multiple services as we had work phone with us as well.)

The parking lot was very wet yesturday, and some of the trail was very slushy. Definitely recommend a waterproof boot/hikers of some sort if the weather is comparable.. If the temperature goes back down in the coming days it's going to make for some icy conditions. 

Lastly, there is a washroom in the parking lot which was a nice bonus, and another part way down the trail. I'm sure there are others as well. Area is well taken care of.. trail signage, washrooms, maps, etc
Spikes needed few areas-stairs totally iced, use trail around n under
Nice to hike on weekend, a lot of ice on the. trails must have Ice treeker.
Beautiful trail! take a right onto the lookout trail after the farm trail in, and the view is amazing - literally could see Toronto! very diverse, lots of wildlife too!

Had a significantly better time now than I did in the fall, for a couple reasons:
1) Do yourself a favour and visit the "Lookout Trail" . I took a detour from the Cliff-Top trail, did the beginning of the Lake loop, and detoured to the Lookout trail there. Then I climbed the Cliff-Top again and finished that. The lookout trail gives you a much more unobstructed view of the cliff-tops.
2) I also detoured a bit and did the spillway trail. It was kinda cool to be in between sections of the escarpment and walking next to them makes you appreciate them more. Certainly more interesting than the total meh of the "Mono Centre" that this trail tries to take you to. Which is nothing.

It also helps that parking seems to be free rather than 16 bucks, though I did buy the Ontario Parks pass anyway this year. Do yourself a favour and bring cramp-ons though. The second set of stairs especially are death traps without 'Em (see pics).
Easy and well maintain trails
We hked on compacted snow. This provided good traction except on steep downhills. These  caused some undignified descents. Beautiful snow scapes.
Easy, great for beginners! Use crampons
Fun hike! Definitely need Crampons. I would call it Easy. Stairs are icy! Watch out. Plenty of parking.
Lovely winter walk - mostly sheltered, with a couple of great lookouts. Just be careful on the stairs if they have snow on them!
Lots of varied terrain with rewarding lookouts.  Look for the less travelled trails.

Very fun trail. Once at the top the view is amazing and worth the trek! Over at the lookout point there are some cliffs which you can climb down (not for everyone) which are super exciting and adds some adventure to the hike! Overall great and enjoyable hike. Ps. Parking tends to fill up fast so go early!
Great view and cool walk through the cliffs
Worth the uphill trek once you see the view!
Great trail
great trail! but wasn't expecting it to be crowded. The whole parking lot was filled as well as the side street towards the entrance of the park
beautiful trail

Mono Cliffs is a lovely park. It's hard to review only one of the trails at the park since we did a few. This one was very nice. Not difficult. Lovely Lake view. We went on the weekend at 9 am and it was fairly empty by the time we were leaving at noon it was absolutely crazy with all the cars parked even on the road. This might be because people are trying to get outside after the covid lock down... not sure. I'd go back and do the entire park again but I'd definitely go in the morning again.
Great trail to start off our hiking season! Well maintained and easy to navigate.
